what_was_done: Checked at the second confirmation. The case the finding probed is fixed and tested. A stale record whose cmd lock is free no longer kills anything, and test_stale_command_group_survives_the_restart fails against the unconditional kill. The C1-1 probe was rerun in a scratch copy. command_pgid is now documented in rewrite/spec/records/job.md. But the lock proves less than records/job.md claims. It shows that some process holding the inherited descriptor is alive, not that the recorded group is. A descendant that leaves the group with setsid and keeps its inherited descriptors, as a daemonizing or backgrounded server does when it does not close them, holds <key>.cmd.lock after its group is gone. Two things follow. The next worker for that key waits five seconds in _take_cmd_lock and then runs without the lock, yet note_command still records command_pgid. And at a later loss, the escapee's lock authorizes attach's SIGKILL. Probe in a scratch copy: run 1's command started a child that forked, called setsid() and slept. Run 1 succeeded, and the cmd lock stayed held. Run 2 of the same key ran a 1-second command but took 6.3 s and recorded command_pgid. A stale running record naming an unrelated 'sleep 30' group then had that group SIGKILLed (-9) on the next attach. To fix: give each attempt a fresh cmd lock, either by having attach unlink <key>.cmd.lock while it holds the job lock and before it spawns the worker, or by putting the nonce in the name. An earlier attempt's escapee then holds only an unlinked inode, and it neither stalls nor authorizes the next attempt's kill. A worker that runs without the lock records no command_pgid. Before the kill, also check that the group leader is still the one recorded (for example its start time from ps against the record's started), or narrow the claim in records/job.md. Add a test with a descendant that calls setsid and keeps the descriptor: a stale record naming an unrelated group must leave that group alive, and a re-run of the key must not wait five seconds.
